title: Five years of local changes left no clear added Superior-level forecast gain for Michigan-Huron at 1970-2024 issues
abstract: We tested whether Lake Superior level adds six-month forecast information for Michigan-Huron after five years of local monthly changes. Ridge penalties were selected each January using earlier validation targets only. At 660 issue months in 1970-2024, adding Superior reduced mean squared error by 2.61%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -0.56% to 5.96%. RMSE fell from 0.14669 to 0.14476 m. The local five-year model had worse point error than a one-year ordinary least squares benchmark. A shared-penalty check gave a 2.77% gain, with limits of 0.09% to 5.75%; shorter blocks included zero. Thus the primary test gives no clear added gain, but it does not show that longer local memory explains earlier gains. Revised data, penalty selection, omitted water-budget terms and conditional intervals limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an independent numerical audit are included. External records are retrieved or regenerated outside the signed package.

display.caption: Added Superior-level skill in four matched models and annual errors in the primary five-year model. Intervals condition on saved forecasts. Shared penalty uses the own-model penalty in both fits.
